items.title: Gear menu (Settings, Help, Report a bug)
items.summary: The narrow left rail used to show a bug button, a help button and the settings gear. Now the rail keeps only the gear and your avatar, and the gear opens one small menu with everything else.

features.name: One gear menu
features.what: Before: three separate buttons in the rail footer (Report a bug, Help, Settings). Now: only the gear and the avatar stay; clicking the gear opens a menu with Settings... (Cmd+,), Help and Report a bug (Cmd+Shift+B). The original buttons are only hidden, so each menu item just clicks the real one.
features.how: Click the gear. Use the arrow keys, Enter, Esc or the first letter of an item. Shift+click on the gear opens Settings directly. When the project sidebar is expanded, its own gear and avatar open the same menu.

items.title: Profile page and Settings API
items.summary: Settings gets a new RE-TEMPO group in its left list, and its first page is Profile: your photo and a calm, read-only summary of your own work. The mod also offers a small API so other mods can add their own Settings pages.

features.name: RE-TEMPO group in Settings
features.what: Before: Settings had only Personal items (Preferences, Chat, Billing...) and Organizations. Now: a RE-TEMPO group sits right after Personal, with Profile first and any page added by other mods (such as Decision model) below it. It uses the same look as the original items.
features.how: Open Settings and click an item under RE-TEMPO. For mod authors: window.__RE_TEMPO_SETTINGS__.registerSection({ id, label, render }).

items.title: Decision model settings (TypeSafe Jev)
items.summary: A new Settings page connects a hosted decision model (TypeSafe AI, "Jev") that answers short typed questions with a choice, a score or a yes/no and a confidence. RE-TEMPO uses it to sort new comment tasks (effort, ask first, urgency).

items.title: inject-index (load the mods)
items.summary: A small script that adds every mod to the app's index.html, in a fixed order, so the app loads them. It can be run again and again without making duplicates.

features.name: Idempotent mod loader
features.what: Before: the original app loads no mods. Now: one marked block before </body> loads each feature/<mod>.css and .js through ./mod/. It backs up index.html once, removes old or hand-made tags and rewrites only that block.
features.how: node tools/inject-index.mjs [--dry-run] <path to index.html>. --dry-run only prints what would change.

items.title: live-reload (instant updates)
items.summary: A watcher with no dependencies: save a feature/ file and the open RE-TEMPO window updates by itself. CSS changes are swapped in without a reload; JS changes reload the window.

features.name: Hot CSS, reload on JS
features.what: Before: changing the app means rebuilding and restarting. Now: the watcher talks to the app through its debug port, hot-swaps the stylesheet on a .css save (the page keeps its state) and reloads the window on a .js save.
features.how: It starts with tools/start-live.sh. Edit and save any feature/*.js or *.css.

items.title: start-live (one command)
items.summary: One command that sets up and starts the whole live loop: links the mods, injects them, launches RE-TEMPO in its own profile and starts the watcher.

features.name: Start everything in one step
features.what: Before: several manual steps. Now: it links out/renderer/mod to the repo's feature/ folder, runs inject-index, opens RE-TEMPO with a debug port and an isolated profile (your real Tempo data is not touched), then runs live-reload. Ctrl+C stops both.

items.title: bootstrap-local (editable app)
items.summary: Builds the editable copy, RE-TEMPO.app, from your own installed Tempo. Nothing is uploaded and the original app is not changed.

features.name: Make RE-TEMPO.app
features.what: Before: the installed Tempo cannot be edited. Now: the script clones the app, unpacks app.asar into a folder, renames it to RE-TEMPO (own bundle id), turns off auto-update, re-signs it and writes run-isolated.sh to start it in its own profile.
features.how: Run scripts/bootstrap-local.sh once, with Tempo installed in /Applications.

items.title: QA harness (qa/)
items.summary: An automated test kit that starts several isolated RE-TEMPO copies, drives them through the debug port, and writes a report with screenshots. It never touches your visible window or your real profile.

features.name: Multi-instance test runner
features.what: Before: no automated tests. Now: run.mjs launches N isolated instances (or logged-in test profiles) in parallel, runs a suite on each, and saves a JSON and Markdown report with screenshots. ps.mjs and clean.mjs list and clean the instances.
features.how: cd qa && npm install, then node run.mjs --suite 00-smoke --instances 3. Details in docs/qa/03-harness.md.
